जब गांव की सड़क पर एक लड़के ने रोका, तब जाकर समझ आया कि शो कितना बड़ा हिट हो चुका है! 😮

पत्रकारिता की नौकरी छोड़कर Mumbai आए actor Chandan Roy को 2020 में आई web series Panchayat से बड़ा ब्रेक मिला था। 🎬

Hindustan Times को दिए इंटरव्यू में Chandan Roy ने बताया कि Covid-19 के दौरान वो अपने गांव Mahnar में थे।

चाचा की बाइक पर आटे की बोरी ले जाते वक्त एक लड़के ने उन्हें रोककर Panchayat में काम की तारीफ की और selfie ली।

Chandan Roy ने बताया कि अब वो 'Hero ka dost' जैसे typecast रोल से बचते हैं और अपनी पसंद से किरदार चुनते हैं।

उन्होंने Raghubir Yadav की तारीफ की कि वो आज भी बोर्ड एग्जाम की तरह हाथ में पेंसिल लेकर script पढ़ते हैं। 🍿

हाल ही में Chandan Roy की short-film Aakhri Ride यूट्यूब चैनल Oh Short Flips पर रिलीज़ हुई है।

क्या आपने Panchayat में Chandan Roy की एक्टिंग देखी है, आपको उनका किरदार कैसा लगा? कमेंट्स में जरूर बताइए! 👇

ctx.title: Panchayat's Chandan Roy recalls how a boy asking for selfie in his village made him realise the show was a hit
ctx.summary: Actor Chandan Roy realised Panchayat had reached beyond major cities when a fan stopped him in his Bihar village to praise the show and ask for a selfie.
ctx.text:
Actor Chandan Roy moved to Mumbai after leaving his full-time journalism job to pursue his dream of becoming an actor. After spending a year taking up small television roles, he got his big break with the web series Panchayat , which premiered in 2020. Its release coincided with the Covid-19 pandemic, which helped the show reach a wider audience and become one of the most popular show on OTT.
In an exclusive interaction with Hindustan Times, Chandan spoke about the exact moment he realised Panchayat had become a hit and that his life was about to change. He also opened up about the fear of being typecast and what he learnt from sharing screen space with veteran actor Raghubir Yadav.
When Panchayat released, Covid was going on. I had gone back to my village. I was holding a sack of flour behind my uncle, who was driving his bike. There, a guy came running up to me. He stopped us and said, "Bhaiya, I just watched your show Panchayat; you did such great work in it." I thought Panchayat would only be watched in big cities like Mumbai and Delhi, but when this kid in a small town like Mahnar came running to me, I felt that something big had happened because Panchayat had reached all the way here. My uncle was also astonished. That kid took a selfie with me, and then I was stopped by another person during that ride.
Initially, when you don't have work and money, and you have to run your kitchen, you don't pay attention to what the character is, whether you even speak in the entire film or if you have a proper scene. But when you get recognition, you can choose whether you want to do a character or not. So, now I am at a stage where I can select or reject a character according to my preference. Now, I tend to avoid characters that I feel will typecast me. For example, I really dislike this character type – 'Hero ka dost'. I feel even if he is the hero's friend, he should have a proper background story.
I never do this because I think my work should be very original, and I should not copy another actor's traits. However, when you work with very senior artists, you definitely observe how they approach a character, how they behave on camera, or how they interact with people on set. So, no doubt, I learn all those things. For instance, I find Raghubir sir's method very beautiful: even today, he prepares with his script as if he's appearing for a board exam. He holds a pencil in his hand, checking, listening and reading every line over and over again. Whenever you go to his room, his script is open on his bed, even at this age and after doing so much work.
Chandan stars in short-film Aakhri Ride , which is presented by Anurag Kashyap and Vasan Bala. It is written and directed by Yashoda Parthasarthy and Vijesh Rajan and produced by Ranjan Singh, Vishesh Agrawal, Rajan EPK and Anurag. It is streaming on the youtube channel Oh Short Flips.
Vibha Maru is an Assistant Editor with Hindustan Times Entertainment, based in Delhi. With a decade of experience across digital and print media, she covers Bollywood, Hollywood and web shows.

A self-confessed cinephile who breathes Hindi cinema, Vibha can often be found sacrificing sleep after binge-watching films and web series. Though she holds a Commerce degree, she discovered her true calling in journalism after enrolling at the Indian Institute of Mass Communication (IIMC). She began her career covering Delhi's cultural scene, food, nightlife, concerts, and city life at The Times of India, before moving into full-time entertainment journalism with India Today.

At India Today, Vibha interviewed some of the biggest names in Bollywood and television while carving a niche for herself through film reviews, opinion pieces, nostalgic features, celebrity interviews, and trend-driven stories. She later brought her storytelling and editorial expertise to The Indian Express, where she continued to deepen her understanding of cinema through long-form entertainment explainers, retrospectives and feature writing
